lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Here's what I can't quite work out, Trophonius, Amphilochus — you're dead. Demonstrably, completely dead. And yet somehow you've been granted temples, you're considered oracles, and the more credulous end of the human population has got it into their heads that you're gods.
lines.note: Menippus opens with the tone of a man reading from a very puzzling spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: Amphilochus
lines.text: And how exactly is that our fault? If people are foolish enough to form opinions like that about dead men, what are we supposed to do about it?
lines.note: Amphilochus: genuinely aggrieved. He has a point, which makes Menippus's next line funnier.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They wouldn't have formed those opinions if you hadn't spent your lives performing exactly that kind of spectacle — claiming to foresee the future, claiming to give oracles on demand. You started it.
lines.note: Flat. No accusation in the voice, just cause and effect.

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: Amphilochus can answer for himself on his own account. As for me — I am a hero, Menippus. I give oracles. Anyone who descends to my sanctuary may consult me. [pause] You clearly have never visited Lebadeia, or you wouldn't be so sceptical.
lines.note: Trophonius delivers 'I am a hero' with the measured dignity of a man reading his own Wikipedia article.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Sorry — are you telling me that unless I actually go to Lebadeia, dress up in that ridiculous linen outfit, crawl through that narrow little hole into the cave clutching a barley cake in both hands — unless I do all of that, I couldn't possibly know that you're dead? Dead, exactly like the rest of us, with the sole distinction that your fraud is better organised?
lines.note: Menippus: not outraged — genuinely curious, in the way that makes things worse. Beat, then the follow-up.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: While I have you, though — what actually is a hero? I'm asking in good faith. I genuinely don't know.
lines.note: The 'in good faith' is the joke.

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: A composite of human and divine.
lines.note: Delivered with the confidence of a man who has given this answer many times and found it satisfactory.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So — not human, as you say. Not divine either. Both simultaneously. [pause] Where has the divine half of you got to, exactly? Right now. I'm looking at you.
lines.note: Menippus peers at him with genuine, unhurried interest.

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: It is giving oracles, Menippus. In Boeotia.
lines.note: Said with total seriousness. This is the problem.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I have no idea what you're talking about. [pause] What I can see, with complete clarity, is that you are entirely, thoroughly, one hundred percent dead.
lines.note: Final line: not unkind. Just a verdict. Menippus has the same expression he started with.
